content.facts: The kind of damage must be reasonably foreseeable; the precise sequence or manner need not be foreseeable.
questionsBeforeCourt: What legal rule governs the doctrine?
content.ratioDecidendi: The kind of injury, burning, was foreseeable. The precise manner, an explosion after a lamp fell into the manhole, did not have to be foreseeable. Citation already in this file: [1963] AC 837.
content.holding: The kind of damage must be reasonably foreseeable; the precise sequence or manner need not be foreseeable.
content.relevance: Apply the ratio to the proved facts.
